title: Rethinking UX Metrics With SUPR-Q
intro: NPS and SUS each produce one number with little guidance on what to do next.

learn.title: Four dimensions
learn.text:
**Usability** — ease of use and navigation; the basis for an estimated SUS
**Credibility** — trustworthy, credible, comfortable doing business with
**Loyalty** — likely to recommend (the NPS item) and to return
**Appearance** — attractive, clean, simple presentation

A usable-but-not-trusted result calls for very different research than a trusted-but-hard-to-use one.

try.q: Your score is stable but credibility has fallen. What does the overall number show?
try.explain: Which is why you track each dimension, not just the total.

left.label: One number
items: No pointer to the next step

learn.title: What you can derive
learn.text:
SUPR-Q lets you derive an **NPS** from its built-in recommend item, and an **estimated SUS** from the two usability items.

Two rules:

• Label the SUS figure as **estimated** — it isn't the full 10-item instrument
• Calculate NPS from the recommend item, **never** by converting the SUPR-Q score

try.q: How should you calculate NPS from SUPR-Q?
try.explain: Converting the composite score is not the same measure.

learn.title: Reading the movement
learn.text:
Small score movements are noise. Look at the dimensions, and at what changed in the product between measurements.

And don't compare a product's NPS with the company-wide marketing NPS — different population, different question context, different meaning.

try.q: Why not compare your product NPS with the company's marketing NPS?
options: NPS can't be compared at all
try.explain: The numbers look alike and mean different things.

test.q: What is the main criticism of NPS and SUS here?
options: One number with no guidance on what to do
They take too long to run
They only work for consumer products
test.explain: SUPR-Q points at a specific follow-up.
Trustworthy, credible, comfortable doing business with.

test.q: What must the derived SUS figure be labelled?
test.explain: It comes from two items, not ten.

test.q: What should you track over time?
test.explain: A stable total can hide a falling credibility score.

test.q: Why does a usable-but-not-trusted product need different research?
options: The problem isn't in the interface
test.explain: The follow-up study is a different study.
